skill.name: Must or might: how strongly a writer commits
skill.why: Strong words like must push you. Weak words like might leave wiggle room.
skill.how: Find the must, should or might word. Ask: is it strong, medium or weak?

beats.say: Must is super strong. You get no choice.
Should is medium. It's good advice, but you could say no.
Might and could are weak. It's just possible.
Same for guessing. Will is sure. Might is a maybe.
These are modal words. Persuaders love the strong ones.

encounters.frame: Two letters about the old Bluster Rock jetty appeared in the local paper on the same day.
encounters.text: LETTER 1, from the Save Our Jetty group: The council must not knock down the old jetty. It has stood for a hundred years, and it will certainly stand for a hundred more if it is repaired. Without it, the fishing club will close, the tourists will vanish and the town will lose its heart. Every resident should come to the meeting on Thursday night and make their voice heard, because this decision cannot be undone. Repairs might keep it safe for another ten years, although we can't be sure until more tests are done in February. We will publish every test result on the noticeboard outside the town hall, so that residents can read them for themselves. encounters.frame: The Mightoo found a camper's diary under a rock at Ghost Gum Gorge.
encounters.text: Day 1. We drove in along a dirt track so bumpy that my teeth rattled, and the gorge walls glowed orange in the late afternoon sun. Set up the tent beneath the biggest ghost gum in the gorge. Around midnight, I heard a slow scratching sound on the canvas, right beside my head. It might have been a possum, or it could have been nothing more than the wind dragging a branch across the tent. I didn't dare look. Day 2. This morning, there were small footprints in the dust outside the tent, each one about the size of a twenty-cent coin. They were probably made by a small animal, although the wind had blurred them too much to be sure. The scratching came back after dark, and this time I heard a soft thump on the roof. Day 3. When I woke up, the packet of marshmallows I'd left in my boot was torn open. There were tiny paw prints in the spilt sugar, and curled up asleep in the boot was a ringtail possum, its tail wrapped around the last marshmallow. So that's what the scratching was. It must be the possum. There's no other explanation, and it's still snoring. I've named it Marshmallow.
